title: fix(qwen): bind DashScope routes to Qwen runtime hooks
body:
Refs #171673

## What Problem This Solves

Qwen runtime hooks are skipped when the registry selects `dashscope` provider IDs or `modelstudio-native` endpoint owners, so existing quota-error handling is unavailable through those bindings.

## User Impact

These references now select the registered Qwen runtime hooks. In particular, a DashScope 429 reporting exhausted free credits is classified as billing, as it already is for the canonical Qwen provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Qwen manifest declares `dashscope` and the `modelstudio-native` endpoint class, but its runtime registration lacks both hook bindings. Add them through the existing internal `hookAliases` contract, matching the pattern used by Amazon Bedrock and Volcengine. Native endpoint metadata supplies the owner reference for custom provider IDs; exact registered provider IDs retain precedence.

Scope limit from code review: custom-provider coverage proves selection after Qwen is registered. Cold activation from a custom provider’s native URL remains a separate control-plane gap: the activation planner uses manifest provider/API references, not runtime hook aliases. This binding-only change does not claim to repair that path.

This PR does not change overflow wording or classification. That work belongs to the shared overflow table and is handled separately by #171712.

## Evidence

- Source inspection traced native URL classification through `resolveProviderEndpoint`, runtime preparation's endpoint owner, and `findProviderRuntimeRegistrationInRegistry`; the latter indexes internal hook aliases. Before this change neither `dashscope` nor `modelstudio-native` resolves to Qwen's runtime registration.
- Regression names: `resolves Qwen quota hooks for dashscope` and `resolves Qwen quota hooks for custom-dashscope`. Both use the real Qwen registration and registry selector, then invoke the existing free-credit 429 classifier and expect `billing`; the custom-ID case also uses native endpoint resolution.
- Exact-head changed-test job [115700154625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38517592324/job/115700154625): `provider-registry-selection.test.ts` passed all 14 tests in 17.14 seconds; the DashScope and custom-provider regressions passed in 1199 ms and 5 ms, respectively.
- Changed-file oxlint (core config), oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed. Deslop found no additional cleanup within scope.
- Prescribed Codex autoreview (`--mode branch --max-priority P2`), including the required fixture source metadata: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. A stalled attempt was stopped; the bounded retry completed successfully.
- Exact-head [CI run 38517592324](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38517592324) for `08b584f08a30d27ab567dc1a0e021de43e80ab97`: changed tests, the affected `check-test-types-core-5` shard, production types, and core lint passed. At the 50-minute observation limit, 22 jobs had passed, none failed, and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` plus `check-lint-extensions-2` were still running. The overall CI gate remains pending.
- PR CI is the test gate for the regression, existing tests, typechecks, and repository checks. Local tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No local test timing is claimed.
- Exact LOC: production +1/-0; tests +46/-0; docs +0/-0. The one production line adds the missing bindings; no superseded implementation exists to delete.
